Question: \(AD\) is the median to side \(BC\) in \(\triangle ABC\), with \(AB=7\text{ cm}\) and \(AC=5\text{ cm}\). By how much does the perimeter of \(\triangle ABD\) exceed the perimeter of \(\triangle ACD\) (unit: cm)?
Solution: The difference between the perimeters of the two triangles is \((AB+BD+AD)-(AC+CD+AD)\). Since \(BD=CD\) and \(AD\) is shared, the difference is \(AB-AC=2\).
